learning_outcomes.text: Acquire knowledge of the main circuit diagrams for signal processing used in electronics.
Know the metrics used to evaluate the performance of electronic systems.
Be able to analyze simple circuits to evaluate their functionality and performance.
Know circuit simulation tools and design methodologies.
Be able to design simple signal acquisition and conditioning systems.
Be able to dimension amplification and filtering circuits, both using block diagrams and circuit diagrams at transistor level.
Be able to choose the most suitable circuit topologies for the problem to be solved.
Be able to simulate a circuit to verify its functionality.
Be able to carry out a comparative evaluation of both circuit and block diagram solutions in order to make the best design and development choices.
Be able to express oneself adequately using the appropriate terminology to describe performance specifications and technical requirements of electronic circuits.
Acquire an appropriate technical language that allows them to communicate adequately, especially with specialist interlocutors.
Acquire the skills to obtain and understand the necessary technical information from datasheets, operating manuals and commercial catalogues.
Acquire the ability to update their skills to technological developments, to understand the functioning of new circuit solutions and to adapt to new development systems.

syllabus_topics: References to the theory of circuits and elementary components (resistors, capacitors, diodes, transistors)
Circuits with capacitors (RC network, passive filters)
Circuits with diodes (half-wave rectifier, bridge rectifier, LED and photodiodes)
Circuits with operational amplifiers (inverting, non-inverting, adder, subtractor) and related non-idealities
Physical realization of logic gates: static and dynamic concepts
Architectures and operating principles of processors
Use of laboratory instruments (signal generator, oscilloscope, multimeter, power supply, breadboards)
Creation and testing of simple analog circuits based on operational amplifiers and their characterization
Notes on the design and manufacturing of printed boards
teaching_methods: Lab sessions using teaching electronic kits
assessment_rules: The assessment is based on a written test (4 analysis/design exercises, 3 hours) and an oral test. The final grade is the arithmetic average of the two tests' scores (out of 30), requiring at least 15/30 in the written test to access the oral part. Alternatively, students can take two intermediate tests, each including 4 exercises (3 hours), with the final grade being the arithmetic mean of their results; a score of at least 15/30 is required in each intermediate test. Laboratory activities are evaluated through quizzes, yielding a score from -1 to 2 added to the final exam/intermediate test grade if it's at least 18/30. Mandatory laboratory attendance (max 25% absences) is required to pass the exam.
